ops.title: #1 TOCTOU: reachability re-assessed (backstop gap, not a first-order exploit) + fix direction
ops.body:
Follow-up to the CONFIRMED bind-source TOCTOU refuter (note f65d5cd) with a cited audit of hermes-agent's actual bind behavior (github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent, `tools/environments/docker.py` DockerEnvironment). Changes the SEVERITY assessment.

## What legitimate code-exec actually binds (cited)
- The LLM-callable surface (`terminal_tool`, `execute_code`) has NO volume/mount/host_cwd parameter — the agent cannot specify a bind Source through any tool argument.
- The code-exec container gets NO docker access: `docker_forward_env=[]` (DOCKER_HOST not forwarded) and no docker.sock mount (forbiddenDest would block it anyway). So LLM code running inside the sandbox cannot issue its own docker-create requests to the proxy.
- Legitimate mounts are a small FIXED set, computed server-side, not agent-influenced: with `container_persistent` defaulting TRUE, `{HERMES_HOME}/sandboxes/docker/<task_id>/{home,workspace}` → /root,/workspace; plus RO credential/skills/cache mounts under HERMES_HOME. `task_id` collapses to the literal "default" for normal agent turns.

## Severity re-assessment
The TOCTOU is a CONFIRMED real mechanism (create-time check vs start-time symlink resolution), but it is **NOT reachable by prompt-injection or code-exec alone** — the untrusted LLM/sandboxed-code has no way to submit a bind mount with a controlled source to the proxy. It is a **defense-in-depth backstop gap**: reachable only by an attacker who has ALREADY escaped the code-exec sandbox (gVisor in tart / micro-VM in B) to the agent-PROCESS trust level, at which point the TOCTOU defeats the docker-proxy backstop and reads the host FS (tart: the VM's secrets; B: the Mac host's /Users/yasyf sops key). The proxy's own threat model (hermes.nix:629, "every code-exec container is a potential escape vector") treats post-escape as in-scope, so it IS a real gap in that last layer — but it is NOT the one-step prompt-injection exploit an earlier framing implied.

## Fix direction (supersedes "reject all binds")
"Reject all binds" would break persistent-mode code-exec (the sandbox /root,/workspace mounts are on the same `docker run` that starts the container). Instead:
1. Proxy validates bind Source against a small FIXED ALLOWLIST (the sandbox `{home,workspace}` pair for task_id=default, operator-configured docker_volumes/extra_args, and the HERMES_HOME-contained RO credential/skill/cache paths) — NOT "any descendant of BIND_ROOTS".
2. Those allowlisted mountpoints are made ROOT-OWNED (every parent path component non-agent-writable), agent-writable LEAF content only — so a compromised agent has no symlink component to flip across create→start. This is codex's broker-provisioned-root fix, narrowed to the actual fixed mount set.

## New complexity surfaced (needs resolution before the fix is concrete)
In Architecture B the agent runs in a CONTAINER while the docker daemon (apple/container) runs on the HOST — DIFFERENT path namespaces. The agent computes bind Sources from HERMES_HOME = its container path (/var/lib/hermes/.hermes/...), but the daemon resolves paths in the host namespace. So B's nested code-exec mounts need path translation or a shared-path arrangement; the prototype only partially validated the nested-sandbox path (E1). The fix design depends on nailing down B's nested-sandbox path model.

Linked: [[container-hermes supervisor + egress pf: codex security review outcomes (2026-07-18)]] (f65d5cd).
